frames.narration: The application commits a transaction that changes rows in two Paxos groups, for example a customer in group 1 and a campaign in group 2. It sends its writes to the leader of group 1, which takes locks for the rows it owns (two-phase locking).

The transaction spans two groups, so their leaders run two-phase commit. Group 1's leader is the coordinator and group 2's leader is a participant. The participant locks its rows and writes a prepare record to its own Paxos group, and then tells the coordinator it is ready.

The coordinator now picks the commit timestamp. It asks TrueTime for an interval that is guaranteed to hold the true time, and takes the latest end of it as the timestamp. The uncertainty is about 4 ms most of the time.
The commit decision is replicated by Paxos to a majority of the replicas of the coordinator's group, in other zones, and the participant is told the decision and the timestamp.

Commit wait. The coordinator does not tell the application the transaction committed until TT.after(timestamp) is true, so the timestamp is certainly in the past on every server. The wait is at least twice the uncertainty, and overlaps with the Paxos messages.

Locks are released and the application is told the transaction committed. Any transaction that starts after this reply, on any server in the world, will pick a larger timestamp, so the order by timestamp matches real time.

A report reads the customer and the campaign together. It picks a timestamp and reads at a replica that has caught up to that time, taking no locks. It sees either all of the transaction or none of it, and the writers are never blocked.
